source.title: DeepSpeed Data Efficiency: Improving Deep Learning Model Quality and Training Efficiency via Efficient Data Sampling and Routing
source.authors: Cong-Long Li; Z. Yao; Xiaoxia Wu; Minjia Zhang; Connor Holmes; Cheng Li; Yu-Xiong He

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures validation perplexity over training tokens for fixed-size GPT-3 runs, but does not fit or assess a scaling-law form.
record.gate_note: Figure 5 reports token-wise validation perplexity for GPT-3 1.3B baseline and combined CL+random-LTD runs. This bears on the loss-versus-token part of V1 only. The paper does not fit a power law or test parameter-count or compute scaling; its downstream accuracy results are not tests of predictability.
record.test_reason: This is a data-efficiency methods paper (curriculum learning plus random-LTD). It fits no scaling law, compares no model sizes and tests no compute allocation, extrapolation or shape. Figure 5 shows within-run validation-perplexity training curves for one 1.3B model, not loss against dataset size. Kaplan et al. appear only in an appendix discussion (A.6), where the authors call their work orthogonal to the scaling laws. Baseline downstream accuracy at several data budgets is a by-product, with learning rates rescaled for each budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase reflects only appendix A.6. The paper's main conclusion is that composing curriculum learning with random-LTD gives up to 12.5x data/cost saving at 95% quality, or 2x saving at equal quality, for GPT-3 1.3B and BERT-large. In A.6 the authors also say the work is orthogonal to Kaplan et al. and that the data/performance relationship still holds.
record.recipe_differences: This paper evaluates data-sampling and token-routing methods rather than fitting scaling laws or reproducing the original scaling-law measurement procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: For baseline GPT-3 1.3B, average 0-shot accuracy over 19 tasks rises with training tokens: 34.5 (3B), 36.3 (6B), 37.2 (12B), 38.8 (24B), 39.8 (48B), 41.5 (96B), 42.0 (150B), 41.9 (200B), 42.5 (300B) (Tables 3, 8). Peak LR was rescaled for each budget. No fit was made, and the curve is non-monotonic between 150B and 200B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed model size, downstream accuracy rises roughly log-linearly with training tokens over two orders of magnitude (untested as a power law).

record.problems: For the loss-versus-token result, only GPT-3 1.3B is shown; the paper gives curves without numerical values or uncertainty and does not fit a power law. It does not test parameter or compute scaling or small-run extrapolation.

untested.parts: All parts: no loss-vs-parameters/tokens/compute fit, and no range of scales measured for loss.
All parts. ViT and GPT-2 finetuning are method comparisons with no scaling measurement.
All parts. Downstream accuracy is reported at several data budgets, but predictability is not assessed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label is removed. Within-run perplexity curves and method-vs-baseline comparisons do not test power-law loss scaling. The baseline data-budget accuracy series is recorded under fits_no_version, not as a test of V6.

versions.untested_parts: Only the token/loss relationship is measured, for GPT-3 1.3B runs. Power-law fit and behavior across several orders of magnitude are not tested; parameter-count and compute relationships are not tested.

rows.subject: GPT-3 1.3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured token-wise validation perplexity during pretraining.
rows.note: The curve is shown, but no numerical perplexity values or explicit power-law fit are reported.
rows.check: This is a single training run's perplexity-vs-step curve, not held-out loss across dataset or model scale. It bears on no version, and no values are reported.

rows.subject: GPT-3 1.3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured token-wise validation perplexity during pretraining with CL and random-LTD.
rows.note: The authors state that the 100%-data approach has better final validation perplexity than the baseline, but give no numerical value or fitted law.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method against its baseline, which is not a scaling-law measurement.

rows.subject: GPT-3 1.3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured token-wise validation perplexity during pretraining.
rows.note: The authors state that baseline training with 50% data does not reach the final validation perplexity of the baseline with 100% data; no numerical values are reported.
rows.check: The only reported fact is that the 150B-token baseline ends with worse perplexity than the 300B-token baseline. Two points with no values, under a different LR schedule, cannot show a power law.

rows.subject: GPT-3 1.3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured token-wise validation perplexity during pretraining with CL and random-LTD.
rows.note: The authors state that this run reaches similar final validation perplexity to the baseline with 300B tokens; no numerical values or power-law fit are reported.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with its baseline, not a scaling-law measurement.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: GPT-3 1.3B validation-perplexity curves across the tested training-token budgets
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports token-wise validation perplexity and says the 150B CL+random-LTD run reaches a similar final value to the 300B baseline (rows F5-base-300B, F5-clr-300B, F5-base-150B, F5-clr-150B); this supports only the tested loss-versus-token relationship, not a power-law form.
